text: Craver distinguishes constitutive from etiological explanation. Explaining long-term memory by identifying the synaptic changes that memory consists in is an example of:
explanation: Explaining a phenomenon by what it consists in (the synaptic changes memory is made of) is constitutive explanation. Etiological explanation cites the causal history that produced it; covering-law explanation subsumes it under general laws; and reverse inference is a neuroimaging inference pattern — none of which is the 'consists in' relation.
